evidence: deepseek-v4-flash uses "Dijkstra from each node to get all-pairs shortest paths"; gpt-oss-120b uses "full = (1 << t) - 1" and "dp = [[INF] * n...", indicating subset-DP Steiner-tree solutions.
affordance_in_statement: An activated rule can be applied an unlimited number of times in any sequence. You may use any of the n variables and apply the activated rules as many times as needed to achieve this.
removal_suggestion: The connectivity/Steiner interpretation is intrinsic and cannot be removed while preserving the current examples, especially Example 1. To re-present it, explicitly restrict which non-target variables may act as relays—for example, state that only variable n may be used as a non-target intermediate—while retaining the existing examples, where variable 4 is the useful relay in Example 1.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Models the problem as a minimum weighted Steiner tree connecting the targets, using all-pairs shortest paths and subset DP.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: You may use any of the n variables and apply the activated rules as many times as needed to achieve this.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Uses a bitmask over the at-most-10 targets and a DP indexed by target subsets and graph vertices, which is the standard Steiner-tree algorithm.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: You may use any of the n variables and apply the activated rules as many times as needed to achieve this.

common_affordance: The activated rules form an undirected connected subgraph containing all targets, with arbitrary non-target variables allowed as Steiner relay vertices.

defeated_student_causes.why_failed: Its visible Kruskal/DSU approach treats the answer as an ordinary MST-style connection problem and does not correctly optimize over non-target Steiner relay vertices.
It sorts edges and uses a DSU/MST-style strategy, which can overpay because the minimum solution need not be an MST on the targets or on all vertices.

recommended_edit: Replace the unrestricted relay permission with an explicit relay eligibility rule, such as: "A variable that is not a target may be used as an intermediate only if it is variable n; all other non-target variables may not be used to transfer values." This preserves the shown examples because Example 1 uses variable 4 as its relay, but defeats the unrestricted Steiner-tree reduction.
regression_risk: qwen3-coder and glm-5 could become correct on restricted instances where the only permitted relay is unnecessary or where the restricted optimum happens to coincide with their MST calculation.
